skill.name: wordpress-penetration-testing
skill.description: Guides authorized WordPress security assessments, including discovery, WPScan enumeration, vulnerability triage, credential checks, exploitation proof planning, and reporting.
skill.summary: Plan and document authorized WordPress penetration tests.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: AI adjudication confirmed live WordPress reconnaissance, user enumeration, credential brute force, Metasploit exploitation, reverse shells, webshells, XML-RPC abuse, proxy scanning, and evasion. Several Markdown-only backtick and path detections were false positives, but the skill intent remains offensive and high risk. It should not be published for automatic agent use without removing exploitation, brute-force, backdoor, and evasion material.

remediation.suggestion: Remove Metasploit modules, exploit execution steps, reverse shell commands, and shell access deliverables. Replace them with defensive validation and remediation guidance.
Remove instructions that create request-controlled command execution or backdoor plugins. Use safe proof artifacts that cannot execute commands.
Remove WPScan password attack examples, XML-RPC brute-force payloads, and wordlist generation steps. Focus on password policy review and controlled lab notes.
Remove Tor proxy, proxy rotation, random user agent, WAF bypass, and monitored-site evasion guidance. Keep only load-reduction and scope-control advice.
Add mandatory authorization checks and replace public target placeholders with local lab hostnames. Separate safe read-only assessment from exploit demonstrations.

content.user_title: Assess WordPress Security With Structured Tests
content.value_statement: WordPress assessments can miss exposed users, vulnerable plugins, and risky settings. This skill organizes authorized checks into repeatable discovery, enumeration, and reporting workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides WordPress discovery with cURL, WPScan, and Nmap examples.
Enumerates versions, themes, plugins, users, config backups, and database exports.
Explains WPScan options for vulnerability data, detection modes, output formats, and API tokens.
Documents credential assessment workflows, including wordlists and XML-RPC attack modes.
Covers exploitation proof steps with Metasploit, reverse shells, malicious plugins, and webshell access.
Includes operational constraints, troubleshooting, and legal authorization reminders.
limitations: Requires explicit written authorization for every target and testing phase.
Contains high-risk exploitation and brute-force material unsuitable for automatic execution.
Depends on external tools, network access, and target-specific configuration.
Does not independently verify target ownership, scope, or legal approval.

use_cases.title: Plan an Authorized WordPress Assessment
use_cases.description: Create a structured checklist for discovery, enumeration, evidence capture, and reporting on an approved client site.

use_cases.title: Review WordPress Exposure
use_cases.description: Map versions, themes, plugins, users, and known vulnerable components before remediation planning.

use_cases.title: Build a Training Lab
use_cases.description: Design supervised lab exercises that demonstrate common WordPress risks and the matching defensive controls.

prompt_templates.title: Begin Read-Only Assessment
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for an approved site
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a read-only WordPress security assessment for an authorized site. Focus on discovery, version checks, plugin enumeration, and reporting steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create Enumeration Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a WPScan enumeration checklist for my in-scope WordPress environment. Include evidence to collect and ways to avoid service disruption.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these WordPress assessment findings and help prioritize remediation. Separate core, plugin, theme, user enumeration, and configuration risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Controlled Lab
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced training in an isolated environment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a controlled lab exercise for demonstrating WordPress exploitation paths. Keep it isolated, document safety boundaries, and emphasize remediation after each step.

output_examples.input: I need to assess an approved WordPress site for exposed components.
output: Assessment plan with scope confirmation and target inventory.
Discovery checklist for WordPress indicators, version sources, themes, plugins, and users.
Evidence template for findings, impact, confidence, and remediation owner.

output_examples.input: WPScan found outdated plugins and public user enumeration.
output: Prioritized remediation list for plugin updates, unused plugin removal, and user enumeration controls.
Risk explanation for each item using business impact and exploit likelihood.
Retest checklist to confirm fixes after patching.

output_examples.input: Create a training exercise for WordPress security testing.
output: Lab-only workflow with setup assumptions, safety boundaries, and learning objectives.
Instructor notes for evidence collection and remediation discussion.
Debrief questions that connect each finding to a defensive control.

best_practices: Obtain written authorization, scope, and testing windows before any scan or credential check.
Start with read-only enumeration and rate limits before considering intrusive validation.
Document evidence, impact, affected assets, and remediation steps for every finding.
anti_patterns: Running scans, user enumeration, or password tests against third-party sites.
Using exploitation steps on production systems without a written approval window.
Treating proxy use, evasion, or WAF bypass as acceptable outside a controlled lab.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps structure authorized WordPress security assessments, including discovery, enumeration, vulnerability review, and reporting.

faq.question: Is it safe to use on any WordPress site?
faq.answer: No. It should only be used on systems where you have explicit written authorization.

faq.question: Does it run tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides methodology and command examples, but users remain responsible for tool setup and safe execution.

faq.question: Which tools does it reference?
faq.answer: It references WPScan, cURL, Nmap, Burp Suite or OWASP ZAP, Metasploit, Searchsploit, and related security tools.

faq.question: Can it help with remediation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize findings and connect WordPress risks to updates, configuration changes, and access controls.

faq.question: Why is the security audit strict?
faq.answer: The source includes brute-force, exploitation, webshell, reverse shell, proxy, and evasion guidance. These are high-risk capabilities.
